gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 7?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from models including GFS and ECMWF indicate a stable high-pressure regime over central Europe will promote clear to partly cloudy skies and light southerly winds over Munich on September 7, supporting maximum temperatures near 27–28 °C. These values align with the market’s leading outcomes at 49 % and 30.5 % implied probability, respectively, and sit well above the 1991–2020 average high of 21 °C for the date. Ensemble guidance shows limited spread, with only modest potential for 29 °C under stronger insolation or slight model warm bias. No significant frontal passage or increased cloud cover is expected before peak heating hours, keeping lower-probability outcomes below 26 °C or above 29 °C at under 15 % combined. Updated model runs through the evening of September 6 will provide the final refinement before resolution.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent model consensus points to a peak temperature in Munich on September 8 driven by warm southwesterly flow, clear to partly cloudy skies, and strong daytime insolation under high pressure.** Multiple forecasts, including ICON, ECMWF guidance, and local outputs, indicate afternoon highs near 29–31°C (roughly 84–88°F), with hourly profiles showing peaks around 30–31°C under light winds and low humidity. This places the market-implied odds for 31°C (40.5%) and 32°C (36.5%) in close contention, reflecting small but meaningful differences in model timing of any residual cloud or exact boundary-layer mixing. Historical September averages hover near 21°C, so the current warm anomaly stems from a transient ridge rather than a prolonged heatwave. Traders are watching the next ECMWF and DWD runs for refinements, as even modest shifts in forecast maxima or dew points could tip probabilities between the two leading outcomes before resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Model consensus shows limited potential for higher readings absent unexpected clearing, while historical September averages around 20°C provide context for the mild but not exceptional values. Updated afternoon observations or any late-day breaks in cloud could refine the final recorded high before resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This outcome aligned closely with National Weather Service model guidance issued the prior evening and fell within the climatological range for early September, when average highs near 79°F are tempered by seasonal cooling trends. Trader consensus converged rapidly once preliminary climatological data (CF6 reports) confirmed the reading, reflecting high confidence in the verified station measurement. Only an unforeseen station calibration error or use of an alternate site would realistically alter resolution.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and model guidance indicate a high of 82–83°F as the most probable outcome for September 8 in New York City, driven by northwest flow under building high pressure that limits cloud cover and moisture while allowing modest daytime heating. Forecast highs cluster in the low 80s across ensemble runs, consistent with the market’s 47% implied probability for that bin and 29.5% for 80–81°F, reflecting trader alignment with official outlooks rather than climatological averages near 79°F. Partly cloudy skies and light winds are expected to prevent significant afternoon warming or cooling, with low precipitation risk supporting the tight distribution around these values. Updated model cycles and any late adjustments to boundary-layer moisture will be the next key data points before resolution.

Updated JMA forecasts and next model cycles will be key near-term catalysts.

Updated model runs and observational data through the morning of the 8th remain the key near-term catalysts.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models from DWD, ECMWF, and GFS indicate a peak temperature near 30–32 °C in Munich on September 8, 2026, under clear skies and southerly flow.** This warm-air advection combined with strong September insolation and minimal cloud cover supports the market’s heavy weighting toward 32 °C (54 % implied probability). Light winds and dry conditions limit mixing and evaporative cooling, reinforcing the upper end of the distribution. Traders are pricing in limited downside risk from overnight model shifts, with resolution hinging on official DWD observations the following day.

Persistent southerly flow advects humid air while afternoon convection develops, capping surface temperatures near or slightly below seasonal normals. Model consensus clusters around 27–29°C, with slight upward bias in some runs if breaks in cloud allow more insolation. Resolution hinges on the precise timing and coverage of rain, which official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble spreads continue to refine ahead of the observation window.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus from DWD, ECMWF, and other models points to a maximum of 31–32 °C in Munich on September 8 under clear skies and southerly flow within a ridge of high pressure.** This setup favors strong daytime heating with minimal cloud cover and negligible precipitation risk, pushing temperatures well above the 1991–2020 average high of 20.9 °C. Recent model runs have stabilized around these values, with limited spread in ensemble guidance and no major shifts in the last 24 hours. The 32 °C outcome leads market-implied odds because it aligns with the upper end of current deterministic and statistical forecasts, while 33 °C remains plausible if boundary-layer mixing or downslope warming exceeds expectations. Final resolution will depend on official observations from stations such as München-Nymphenburg.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Clear skies and light northwest winds are driving the tight trader split between 78–79°F and 80–81°F highs in New York City on September 7.** Official forecasts from sources including the National Weather Service and local models converge on mostly sunny conditions with highs near 80°F, supported by strong September solar insolation, low humidity around 40–50% at peak, and minimal cloud cover allowing efficient surface heating. Northwest flow at 5–10 mph provides modest mixing that tempers extreme warming while preventing significant marine influence or afternoon convection. The narrow 1°F spread in leading outcomes reflects genuine uncertainty in the precise timing of maximum temperature, urban heat-island contributions at Central Park or LaGuardia stations, and minor model differences in boundary-layer mixing. With resolution hinging on the official daily maximum, any late-day cloud increase or wind shift could tip the outcome between the two bins.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts from multiple models (including GFS, ICON, and DWD output) point to a high of roughly 20–22°C in Munich on September 9, 2026, aligning with the market’s tight clustering around 21°C (24.5%) and 22°C (30%).** After an unusually warm September 8 (highs near 30–33°C under mostly sunny skies), a cold front and associated low-pressure system are expected to arrive overnight or early on the 9th, bringing widespread cloud cover, showers or thunderstorms (60–85% probability), and west-to-northwest winds of 5–10 m/s.

These conditions limit daytime solar heating and promote cooler air advection and evaporative cooling from rain, capping the maximum temperature. Historical climatology for September 9 shows an average high of ~20.7°C, so the current setup represents a modest cool anomaly driven by the frontal passage rather than extreme deviation.

The narrow spread between 21°C and 22°C (and smaller probabilities for 20°C or 23°C) reflects residual uncertainty in model timing of the front, exact cloud thickness, and whether any brief clearing allows a slightly higher peak before steady rain sets in. Later updates from the National Weather Service equivalents or refined high-resolution runs will likely tighten this range as the event approaches.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast uncertainty over cloud cover, rain timing, and Atlantic air influence is keeping the highest temperature in London on September 8 tightly contested between 19°C and 20°C in trader positioning.** Official guidance from the Met Office and ensemble models points to early rain or showers clearing to sunny spells and breezy westerly winds, with daytime maxima around 21°C but tempered by persistent cloud and limited insolation. Historical early-September baselines near 19–20°C, combined with the current frontal passage, create narrow differentiation: stronger or more prolonged cloud would cap readings at 19°C, while earlier clearance and modest warming could push toward 20–21°C. Updated model runs and observational data through the morning will likely refine these probabilities as the day progresses.

Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models show mostly cloudy skies with occasional thunderstorms, especially in the afternoon, which reduces insolation and favors the lower end of recent climatological norms for early September. Trader emphasis on 29 °C as the slight favorite reflects these stable, moist conditions, while modest probabilities for 28 °C or 30 °C capture uncertainty in exact timing and intensity of any breaks in the cloud deck. Updated model runs and the next JMA briefing will refine the outcome before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Japan Meteorological Agency and international sources indicate a high probability of afternoon showers and thunderstorms over Tokyo on September 9, with highs expected in the 29–32°C range amid elevated humidity and southerly flow. Recent heavy rainfall from a stationary frontal system and typhoon remnants has cooled surface conditions and increased cloud cover, capping potential maxima while raising the chance of localized suppression below 30°C if convection develops earlier. Traders assign the strongest implied probability to 31°C because ensemble guidance shows modest warming potential under partly cloudy breaks, yet wide spreads across 28–33°C reflect model disagreement on precipitation timing and intensity. Historical September baselines near 27–28°C underscore how residual summer warmth and urban effects support the current consensus distribution.
